tryItExercises.title: Let the navigation wrap when space gets tight
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

The navigation works on wide screens, but its links can run out of horizontal room on narrower screens.

**Task**

Keep all existing CSS. Add `flex-wrap: wrap;` to `nav` so navigation items can move onto another flex line when needed.
tryItExercises.hint: The navigation is already a flex container. Add wrapping for the navigation.

help.concept: Flex wrapping lets nav items move to another line when needed, while a column flex form with `gap` creates consistent control spacing without extra markup.
help.hint_1: Apply wrapping to nav and use the existing form as a separate column flex container.
help.hint_2: Narrow the preview and open Contact: nav items should be able to wrap, and the form fields should form a clean vertical flex flow.

tryItExercises.title: Turn the main content into a wrapping flex row
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

The main content still stacks vertically, so the existing semantic cards cannot share a row and wrap naturally.

**Task**

Keep every previous rule. Give `main` `flex-direction: row;`, `flex-wrap: wrap;`, and `gap: 1.5rem;`.
tryItExercises.hint: Change main's direction, allow wrapping, and add the requested gap.

help.concept: A wrapping row lets content cards form responsive lines, while a wrapping footer can distribute its items and still collapse safely when space is tight.
help.hint_1: Both containers already exist; give each the flex behavior appropriate to its content.
help.hint_2: Resize the preview: main content should form flexible rows, and footer items should spread out on wide screens then wrap when necessary.

tryItExercises.title: Build a wrapping footer distribution pattern
tryItExercises.prompt:

The footer items still use ordinary flow and do not take advantage of the available horizontal space.

**Task**

Keep the wrapping main layout. Make `footer` a flex container with `display: flex;`, `flex-wrap: wrap;`, `justify-content: space-between;`, and `gap: 1rem;`.
tryItExercises.hint: Give the footer its own wrapping flex layout, distribution, and spacing.

help.concept: A wrapping row lets content cards form responsive lines, while a wrapping footer can distribute its items and still collapse safely when space is tight.
help.hint_1: Both containers already exist; give each the flex behavior appropriate to its content.
help.hint_2: Resize the preview: main content should form flexible rows, and footer items should spread out on wide screens then wrap when necessary.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: The flex shorthand controls growth, shrink, and basis
sketchBlocks.title: The flex shorthand controls growth, shrink, and basis

tryItExercises.title: Give the content cards a flexible starting size
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

The wrapping content cards can share rows, but they do not yet have a useful flexible basis for readable sizing.

**Task**

Keep the cumulative layout. Give `main > section, main > article` `flex: 1 1 18rem;`.
tryItExercises.hint: Use the grouped selector for the semantic cards and give those flex items a grow, shrink, and basis value.

help.concept: A flex basis gives the semantic cards a useful target `width`, while cross-axis alignment and a non-growing/non-shrinking link flex value stabilize the navigation.
help.hint_1: Use the existing main children as flex items, then finish the nav by controlling alignment and the links' flex behavior.
help.hint_2: Check wide and narrow previews: cards should resize and wrap from an 18rem basis, while nav links remain centered and keep their intrinsic `width`.

tryItExercises.title: Keep each navigation link at its intrinsic flex size
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

Navigation links should keep their content-sized width instead of growing or shrinking unpredictably as flex items.

**Task**

Keep every previous Module 3 change. Add `nav a { flex: 0 0 auto; }`.
tryItExercises.hint: Set the nav link's grow and shrink factors to zero and let its basis come from its own size.

help.concept: A flex basis gives the semantic cards a useful target `width`, while cross-axis alignment and a non-growing/non-shrinking link flex value stabilize the navigation.
help.hint_1: Use the existing main children as flex items, then finish the nav by controlling alignment and the links' flex behavior.
help.hint_2: Check wide and narrow previews: cards should resize and wrap from an 18rem basis, while nav links remain centered and keep their intrinsic `width`.
